subject.title: [Feature]: Add an optional result-return mode for /hooks/agent

question: Should OpenClaw accept a first-class synchronous result-return contract for `POST /hooks/agent`, and if so should it return raw agent text/errors or a bounded/redacted result envelope with explicit audit semantics?
rationale: The source gap is clear and an implementation candidate exists, but the permanent API shape controls externally visible agent output, long-held hook requests, idempotency replay, and whether machine-only successes bypass main-session announcement.

options.title: Accept a bounded result contract
options.body: Land the feature only after the PR wraps or caps returned output/errors and documents the audit behavior for suppressed success announcements.

options.title: Use a separate sync/result endpoint
options.body: Ask the PR to move the blocking/result path to a dedicated endpoint or result-token fetch flow if that gives a cleaner security boundary than extending `/hooks/agent`.

options.title: Keep async-only hooks
options.body: Decline the core API addition and keep `/hooks/agent` plus `sessions_history` polling as the supported machine callback pattern for now.

recommendation.title: Accept a bounded result contract
recommendation.body: Land the feature only after the PR wraps or caps returned output/errors and documents the audit behavior for suppressed success announcements.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has adjacent gateway hook history and is one of the reviewers explicitly requested in the linked implementation discussion.
